title: System Architecture
lead: The component map, the wake-up stack, and the non-negotiable design principles.
summary: MemPalace is a multi-layer AI memory system built on a pluggable storage backend (ChromaDB default) plus a SQLite knowledge graph. User data flows through miners into verbatim drawers, indexed by AAAK-compressed closets. The L0-L3 wake-up stack injects context on demand: identity plus essential story (~600-900 tokens), on-demand wing/room retrieval, and deep semantic search. Every component honors five non-negotiable principles: verbatim-always storage, append-only ingestion, local-first execution, background hooks, and privacy by architecture.

concepts.definition: A broad category (person, project, topic) that groups related memory. Drawers are organized under wings.
A time-based or topic-based grouping within a wing (e.g., a day, a session, a discussion thread). Drawers live in rooms.
A single chunk of verbatim user content (never summarized or paraphrased). The atomic storage unit that is queried, ranked, and returned in search results.
A searchable index layer using AAAK compression. Stores topic pointers, entity names, and quote fragments - scanned by LLM to identify relevant drawers without reading all content.
Lossy symbolic compression format (entities, topics, emotions, flags) that lets an LLM scan thousands of closet entries instantly and know exactly which drawer to open.

Four memory layers: L0 (user identity), L1 (essential story auto-generated from palace), L2 (on-demand wing/room retrieval), L3 (deep semantic search). L0+L1 inject ~600-900 tokens; L2/L3 add context on demand.
Pluggable storage interface (base.py). ChromaDB is the default reference implementation; custom backends subclass BaseBackend and BaseCollection.
SQLite-backed temporal entity-relationship graph. Stores (subject, predicate, object) triples with valid_from/valid_to dates for entity-first reasoning.

symbols.name: MemoryStack
symbols.role: Unified interface to the 4-layer wake-up stack (L0 identity, L1 essential story, L2 on-demand retrieval, L3 deep search)

symbols.name: search_memories
symbols.role: Main entry point for hybrid semantic + BM25 search across the palace; returns ranked drawers with metadata

symbols.name: get_collection
symbols.role: Factory to fetch or create a collection (mempalace_drawers default) through the backend layer; lazy-initializes on first access

symbols.name: build_closet_lines
symbols.role: Generates AAAK closet pointer lines from drawer content (topics, entities, quotes, dates). I18n-aware entity extraction.

symbols.name: ChromaBackend
symbols.role: Reference RFC 001 backend implementation wrapping ChromaDB with HNSW tuning, segment health checks, and Windows-safe locking

symbols.name: KnowledgeGraph
symbols.role: SQLite-backed temporal entity-relationship graph; stores and queries (subject, predicate, object) triples with valid_from/valid_to dates

symbols.name: mine_palace_lock
symbols.role: Per-palace non-blocking lock protecting concurrent mine operations; re-entrant, with holder identity recording

symbols.name: Layer0
symbols.role: Reads user identity from ~/.mempalace/identity.txt; ~100 tokens, always loaded in wake-up

symbols.name: Layer1
symbols.role: Auto-generates essential story from highest-weight palace drawers; ~500-800 tokens, grouped by room

symbols.name: BaseBackend
symbols.role: Abstract RFC 001 backend interface; subclass to implement custom storage (ChromaDB, Weaviate, Pinecone, etc.)

symbols.name: file_already_mined
symbols.role: Checks if a file's drawers exist at the current NORMALIZE_VERSION; triggers silent schema upgrades on version mismatch

symbols.name: NORMALIZE_VERSION
symbols.role: Schema version for drawer normalization; stale drawers are silently rebuilt when miner encounters older version

surprises.title: Closets Are Ranking Signals, Never Gates
surprises.detail: The architecture explicitly forbids using closets as filters. A weak or missing closet pointer cannot hide a drawer that has strong BM25 signal. Closets only contribute a boost weight, so weak closets can only help search, never harm it - the opposite of typical RAG index designs.

surprises.title: Verbatim Always: Even Newlines and Formatting Preserved
surprises.detail: No summarization, paraphrasing, or lossy compression of drawer content. CLAUDE.md (line 22): 'If a user said it, we store exactly what they said.' This extends to whitespace, code formatting, and even Unicode surrogate pairs (handled by strip_lone_surrogates for Windows clipboard corruption).

surprises.title: Lock Holder Identity Recorded in Lock File
surprises.detail: When a mine holds the palace lock, the lock file body records the PID and first 3 argv entries (e.g., 'PID 12345 mempalace mine ~/palace'). If another mine contends, it reads this identity and includes it in the MineAlreadyRunning error message, so users see exactly which process is blocking them.

surprises.title: Re-entrant Lock Tracking Per Thread + PID
surprises.detail: The system maintains a per-thread threading.local() set of lock keys the current thread holds. When a process forks, this set is inherited, but the PID check clears stale state so children correctly reacquire. This prevents self-deadlock when miner.mine() (outer lock) calls ChromaCollection.upsert() (same lock) from the same thread.

surprises.title: Closet Char Limit Packs Greedily Without Splitting Lines
surprises.detail: Closets are packed greedily up to CLOSET_CHAR_LIMIT=1500 chars, but lines (topic pointers) are never split. If a line would overflow the current closet, it flows to a new closet (_01, _02, ...). This keeps closet pointers grep-friendly and atomic.

surprises.title: L1 Importance Defaults to 3.0, Reads Multiple Field Names
surprises.detail: Layer1.generate() tries four metadata keys in order: 'importance', 'emotional_weight', 'weight', defaulting to 3.0 if none are found. This provides backward compatibility with older schemas and multiple naming conventions. No importance field means all drawers weighted equally, ranked only by order fetched.

surprises.title: BM25 IDF Computed Over Candidate Set, Not Corpus
surprises.detail: BM25 rescoring is applied to the candidate set returned by vector search, not the full palace. IDF is computed locally from the candidates. This is correct for reranking a small set but would be inaccurate over the full palace - a term rare overall but common in the candidate set gets inflated IDF, which is exactly right for discriminating within those results.

surprises.title: Windows File Locking: Byte 0 Only, Position-Dependent
surprises.detail: On Windows, msvcrt.locking() locks a specific byte range at the current file position. Byte 0 is explicitly locked; holder identity is written from byte 1 onward. This prevents collisions between lock acquisition and diagnostic identity reads. The code seeks to position 0 before locking so holders and contenders lock the same byte.

surprises.title: STDOut Redirected to StdErr Before Heavy Imports
surprises.detail: MCP server redirects stdout->stderr at both Python and file-descriptor level before importing chromadb/onnxruntime, because those dependencies print banners and errors directly to stdout (sometimes at C level), breaking Claude Desktop's JSON-RPC parser. Real stdout FD is saved and restored before entering the MCP protocol loop.

designDecisions.decision: Append-only writes with atomic delete+insert per file
designDecisions.rationale: Incremental-only principle (CLAUDE.md line 23): 'Never destroy existing data to rebuild.' File re-mines lock, delete stale drawers for that source_file, then insert fresh ones. A crash during delete leaves drawers with stale normalize_version (triggers re-mine later); a crash during insert leaves new drawers missing but old ones intact. No palace corruption.

designDecisions.decision: Closets as optional ranking boost, never as gates
designDecisions.rationale: 100% recall is non-negotiable. Weak closets (regex-extracted from narrative content) must never hide drawers. Only BM25 + vector distance matter for inclusion; closets add a boost weight. Search accuracy degrades gracefully even if entity extraction fails or closets are stale.

designDecisions.decision: L0+L1 wake-up (~600-900 tokens) injected automatically, L2+L3 on-demand
designDecisions.rationale: Performance budgets (CLAUDE.md line 26): hooks <500ms, startup injection <100ms. Inject minimal context (identity + essentials) automatically. Deeper context (wings, topics, searches) loads on-demand only when the user mentions them, leaving 95%+ of context window free.

Local-first, zero external API by default (CLAUDE.md line 25): embeddings computed by Ollama/LM Studio on localhost. External providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) are BYOK, never required, never silent defaults. Code explicitly checks for configured providers before any fallback; external APIs are never enabled by environmental surprise.

designDecisions.decision: Per-palace locking, non-blocking, with identity recording
designDecisions.rationale: Concurrency safety without resource exhaustion. Per-palace (not global) allows parallel mines on different palaces. Non-blocking prevents daemon pileup. Identity recording lets users diagnose who holds the lock. Thread + PID tracking prevents self-deadlock when nested miners try to acquire the same lock.

related.why: The 4-layer wake-up stack (L0-L3) is the primary external interface to the architecture; injected via MCP/CLI/hooks
Wings, rooms, drawers, and closets are the core data model that every component operates on
Hybrid BM25 + vector search is the retrieval mechanism at L3; closets are ranking signals
Project miner is the primary ingestion path, feeding drawers into the architecture
Entity-first design principle; KG stores relationships extracted from drawers
Local-first, zero external APIs, privacy by architecture - core to system design

searchDoc.title: System Architecture
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace is a multi-layer AI memory system built on a pluggable storage backend (ChromaDB default) plus a SQLite knowledge graph. User data flows through miners into verbatim drawers, indexed by AAAK-compressed closets. The L0-L3 wake-up stack injects context on demand. Every component honors five non-negotiable principles: verbatim-always storage, append-only ingestion, local-first execution, background hooks, and privacy by architecture.
searchDoc.body: MemPalace is a multi-layer AI memory system with three concerns: ingestion (getting data in), retrieval (search and the wake-up stack), and the substrate that holds it (the pluggable storage backend and the SQLite knowledge graph). Ingestion runs through three miners - projects, conversations, and documents - which scan source files, split content into verbatim chunks called drawers, detect entities and wings/rooms, and route each drawer to palace storage. For every drawer the system builds AAAK-compressed closet pointers (topic plus entities plus quotes) so semantic search can locate relevant drawers quickly. All writes are append-only: a re-mine locks the source file, deletes prior stale drawers, then inserts fresh ones, so a crash mid-cycle leaves the palace untouched. Drawers live in the mempalace_drawers collection and closets in a separate mempalace_closets index. Search is hybrid: search_memories queries ChromaDB vector embeddings, gets candidate drawers, then re-ranks them with Okapi-BM25 scored over the candidate set's local corpus IDF. If vector search is disabled, it falls back to ChromaDB's SQLite FTS5 layer. Closets contribute only an optional boost weight - they are ranking signals, never gates - so weak or stale closets can never hide a strong BM25 match. Results are always verbatim drawer text with metadata: wing, room, source file, similarity. The wake-up stack has four layers. L0 is user identity read from ~/.mempalace/identity.txt. L1 is an auto-generated essential story scored by importance and recency, grouped by room, capped at 3200 chars. Together L0 plus L1 cost roughly 600 to 900 tokens and leave 95 percent of the context window free. L2 loads on-demand wing/room retrieval and L3 runs deep semantic search, each lazy and never blocking the chat. The storage backend follows an RFC 001 interface defined in backends/base.py with typed QueryResult and GetResult. ChromaBackend is the default reference implementation, wrapping ChromaDB's PersistentClient with HNSW bloat-guard tuning (batch_size and sync_threshold of 50000) to prevent link_lists.bin from ballooning on large mines. A separate SQLite knowledge graph stores subject-predicate-object triples with valid_from and valid_to dates for entity-first temporal reasoning; entity IDs are SHA256 of the name and triples are immutable. Concurrency is protected by mine_palace_lock, a per-palace, non-blocking, re-entrant lock that records the holder's PID and argv for diagnostics. Design principles are enforced by architecture: verbatim-always, incremental-only, entity-first, local-first embedding with optional BYOK external LLMs, sub-500ms hooks, and privacy by architecture. Background hooks sync new memory asynchronously with zero chat tokens.
